CVE-2026-58266.title: Anki is a program for creating and reviewing flashcards. Prior to ...
CVE-2026-58266.description: Anki is a program for creating and reviewing flashcards. Prior to 25.09.4, Anki's webview-based pages communicate with the Rust backend using an internal localhost API, and user scripts included via iframes in the editor can access this API despite protections intended to block reviewer and editor scripts. A malicious imported card package with an embedded iframe can use exposed API methods such as getImageForOcclusion to read arbitrary files accessible to the Anki process and exfiltrate them over the network. This issue is fixed in version 25.09.4.

CVE-2026-59153.title: Anki is a program for creating and reviewing flashcards. Prior to ...
CVE-2026-59153.description: Anki is a program for creating and reviewing flashcards. Prior to 25.09.3, Anki launches a local HTTP server to serve media files and web pages for parts of its interface, but requests from other origins were not sufficiently blocked. A malicious website could potentially trigger side-effecting requests to the local server, with severity varying by browser depending on Private Network Access protections. This issue is fixed in version 25.09.3.

CVE-2026-64677.title: Anki is a program for creating and reviewing flashcards. Prior to ...
CVE-2026-64677.description: Anki is a program for creating and reviewing flashcards. Prior to 25.09.3, endpoints in Anki's local HTTP server do not adequately constrain requested media and built-in data paths, allowing scripts served from shared decks, or malicious websites combined with an origin-check bypass, to read local files through directory traversal. This issue is fixed in version 25.09.3.

GHSA-gfvm-4968-jp9m.title: macOS Arbitrary Code Execution on Show in Folder
GHSA-gfvm-4968-jp9m.description: ### Summary This is a similar finding to https://github.com/ankitects/anki/security/advisories/GHSA-932p-crhj-v43p An attacker can build a deck that has a card with a custom image source. When a user on macOS clicks 'show in folder' on the image, arbitrary code is executed on the user's system. ### Details The finding is due to AppleScript injection at line 943 of qt/aqt/utils.py. The image source is interpolated directly into AppleScript code. Commit 6eb89c06488 which forces image extensions in filepaths does not prevent this, since a command can be run from a parenthesised expression. ### Impact Arbitrary code execution; macOS users who import and edit malicious decks are affected.

GHSA-m5rf-76jh-mgwp.title: Cross-Site Scripting via Note/Card Type Names in Check Blank Cards
GHSA-m5rf-76jh-mgwp.description: The 'Check Blank Cards' tool (Tools → Check Blank Cards) renders note type and card type names as raw HTML without sanitization. An attacker who can set a malicious name (e.g., `<script>alert('XSS')</script>`) and create a blank card for that type can trigger JavaScript execution when a victim runs the tool. **Demonstrated impacts:** - **Confidentiality:** Exfiltrate files from Anki's media directory by encoding them as base64 and sending them to an attacker-controlled server. - **Integrity:** Tamper with the 'Check Blank Cards' dialog to display falsified results. - **Availability:** Crash or hang the app via a `setInterval` loop.
